thread:
alex: Kicking off the geo-rollout now. US -> EU -> APAC, deploybot will do 5% slices. tagging ops for capacity checks.

deploy-bot: :rocket: Deploy start: release v2.4.1 -> slice 1 (us-west). ETA 6m. Rollout id: r-5298765432.

samantha: Copy. I'll run the capacity smoke for US West and check GPU queue.

jorge: US cpu/gpu headroom looks good. 95th tail latency stable. Sample: p50 80ms, p95 290ms. No retry spikes.

priya: Can we pin EU to v2.3.9 until we validate on US? Want to avoid cross-region drift if we have to rollback.

alex: yeah pin EU. Only allow the canary slice to proceed in EU if we manually lift the pin.

deploy-bot: Slice complete: r-5298765432 slice 1 (us-west) -> healthy. Advancing to slice 2 (eu-west) in 2m.

emily: EU capacity check starting now. Running: `./scripts/load-check --region=eu-west --qps=1200 --duration=3m`

ops-bot: Alert: EU pod eviction rate increased by 2.1x over baseline (last 5m). Investigating node pressures.

emily: Hmm seeing some OOM churn on a few smaller instances, causing kube reschedules. Rolling EU canary to 10% hold.

ken: Suggest reduce burst to 60% for EU slice and run with `--max-batch-size=8`. If that stabilizes, we can continue.

priya: Given the instability, I recommend we hold EU and APAC and only continue US rollout. Pin EU+APAC to v2.3.9 and escalate APAC capacity checks.

alex: Agreed. Alex -> @deploy-bot, cancel EU/ APAC slices and pin them to v2.3.9. Keep US as live.

deploy-bot: Action: cancel slices 3..4 for eu-west & apac-sg. Pin regions: eu-west -> v2.3.9, apac-sg -> v2.3.9. Rollout r-5298765432: partial success.

ops-bot: Rollback executed in apac-sg cluster: rollback id rb-5298765432-apac. APAC traffic diverted to fallback pool.

jorge: APAC metrics: token generation latency jumped (p95) from 380ms -> 1.2s at 22:12 UTC. Error rate up from 0.2% -> 1.8% concurrent with pod churn.

emily: Confirmed restart storms tied to a kernel OOM on t3a-like nodes. Node autoscaler is still adding nodes but pods keep bumping into memory caps.

ken: Temporary mitigation: move APAC routing to dedicated warm pool (capacity reserved) and run a degraded quantized variant (q4_0) for 30m. That should lower memory pressure.

priya: Good call. Apply warm pool and swap model variant to q4_0 for APAC only. We'll monitor quality. If regressions > 3% on eval set, rollback further.

alex: Do it. Also create a rollback trigger: if p95 > 800ms or errors > 1% for 10m, we fully rollback APAC.

deploy-bot: APAC routing change: warm-pool active, model variant set to q4_0 for apac-sg.

ops-bot: Note: we've created incident INC-2026-0412 for APAC instability and linked this thread.

jorge: After warm pool + q4_0, p95 dropped to 470ms within 6m and error rate to 0.6%. Still higher than baseline but acceptable for now.

emily: Running quick eval set against q4_0 responses — minor hallucination increase ~0.8% on a small prompt set. Logging to S3: s3://redwood-evals/apac/q4_0/5298765432.log

priya: Set temporary quality monitor: compare sample outputs against golden set every 10m, alert to #product if >2% regression.

alex: Next steps: 1) Keep US live and continue standard rollout windows. 2) EU pinned until config/instance sizing fix. 3) APAC on warm pool + q4_0 for rolling tests. 4) Postmortem if incident persists > 6h.

ken: I'll follow up with infra to evaluate node sizing and consider c6g vs t3a swap in APAC clusters.

emily: I've documented the quick rollback playbook and added notes to the release notes draft: "APAC: temporary model-variant fallback applied during warm-pool transition".

priya: I'll coordinate with support to surface customer-impacted accounts and prepare comms if we need an expanded rollback.

alex: Thanks all. Reopen this thread if we need to escalate. :thumbsup:
